business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Sustain the Core, Build the Future: protect established electrical-insulation strengths while building capability in emerging applications
- Strengthen presence in established segments (power/transmission electrical insulation) while expanding into emerging applications (e-mobility, electronics, data centres, BESS)
- Integrate innovation, sustainability and digital systems into the operating model, embedded in capital allocation, process design and execution
- Shift from material supplier to solution contributor via value-selling: engaging customers on lifecycle performance, energy implications and broader operational outcomes rather than material specs alone
- Collaboration as an operating model: joint customer visits and basket offerings across product lines instead of segments approaching customers independently
- Leverage the ALTANA/ELANTAS global network for technology transfer, troubleshooting support and access to group expertise to accelerate readiness without duplicating local development
- Platform-led innovation: extend existing chemistries into adjacent applications and selectively transfer ALTANA-network technologies rather than pursue isolated product launches
- Build leadership depth across the organisation to support future growth
- Evaluate future-ready manufacturing expansion through greenfield development and greater automation
- Advance water-based technologies to improve environmental performance while maintaining material reliability
- Strengthen process safety management and pursue energy efficiency, emission reduction and renewable energy opportunities across manufacturing operations
- Board has approved and adopted a Dividend Distribution Policy under Regulation 43A of the SEBI Listing Regulations. Dividend held flat at Rs 7.50 per equity share of Rs 10 each for FY2025, unchanged from FY2024, subject to Members' approval at the AGM. The Board did not propose any transfer to general reserves during the year under review, and share capital remained unchanged during the year. Debt-equity and debt-service/interest coverage ratios are stated as not applicable to the Company, consistent with an internally funded balance sheet.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The Company is setting up a new manufacturing facility at Taluka Vagra, District Bharuch, Gujarat (governmental approvals in process) to synergise, expand and realign its manufacturing operations for future growth. It integrated the Von Roll (India) resin and tapes business into its Pimpri operations, installing capacity for the Von Roll business at Pimpri through technology transfer, and is progressing on technology absorption/localisation of the HV resin business, having commenced manufacturing of 22 new such products at Pimpri. At Ankleshwar, infrastructure improvements de-congested and optimised the Resin Plant, increasing production capacity for PVF wire enamel, with access roads to storage/dispatch areas also improved. During the year, scrubber systems were installed at both Pimpri and Ankleshwar plants to further reduce VOC emissions, DCS rooms and software were upgraded, energy-saving projects (VFDs for cooling-tower pump motors, energy-efficient motor replacements) were executed, and new auto-packing lines were introduced to improve packaging efficiency. For 2026, the Company plans to expand the solvent recovery plant to support increased wire enamel production, which will double recovery capacity after completion. Technical improvements (debottlenecking, automation, Lean Six Sigma/Kaizen/5S) helped meet increased market demand largely without major capital expenditure.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Manufacturing growth in India, supported by domestic consumption, investment trends and rising exports, expected to keep demand aligned with the broader pace of economic growth
- Pace of industrial production in India remains important as it supports electrification, infrastructure development and expansion across key served markets
- Sustained growth in e-mobility, data centres, Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) and other emerging insulation-industry trends expected to create new application areas and demand
- Stability in raw material prices and resilience of global supply chains seen as key to operational efficiency and consistent financial performance
- Rise of renewable energy, data centres and e-mobility increased demand for PVF and higher-temperature-class insulation products in 2025
- Government focus on standards/ratings for appliances (e.g. fans) drove replacement demand as manufacturers cleared older inventory for new-standard products
- Prolonged monsoons reduced demand linked to pumps/rewinding (irrigation); a milder summer reduced demand for coolers and air conditioners
- Sharp increases in copper and aluminium prices in 2025 caused a temporary slowdown; aluminium continued substituting copper in certain low-temperature-class applications on cost/weight grounds, creating demand for specific product-colour solutions
- Exports (small share of sales, mainly Bangladesh and Nepal) saw minimal activity in 2025 due to political instability in those markets
- Increased competition across the value chain, especially when external markets slow, seen as a threat to prices and margins
- Urbanisation around manufacturing locations may raise environmental concerns and evolving compliance requirements

- Manufacturing growth in India, supported by domestic consumption, investment trends and rising exports, expected to keep demand aligned with the broader pace of economic growth
- Pace of industrial production in India remains important as it supports electrification, infrastructure development and expansion across key served markets
- Sustained growth in e-mobility, data centres, Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) and other emerging insulation-industry trends expected to create new application areas and demand
- Stability in raw material prices and resilience of global supply chains seen as key to operational efficiency and consistent financial performance
- Rise of renewable energy, data centres and e-mobility increased demand for PVF and higher-temperature-class insulation products in 2025
- Government focus on standards/ratings for appliances (e.g. fans) drove replacement demand as manufacturers cleared older inventory for new-standard products
- Prolonged monsoons reduced demand linked to pumps/rewinding (irrigation); a milder summer reduced demand for coolers and air conditioners
- Sharp increases in copper and aluminium prices in 2025 caused a temporary slowdown; aluminium continued substituting copper in certain low-temperature-class applications on cost/weight grounds, creating demand for specific product-colour solutions
- Exports (small share of sales, mainly Bangladesh and Nepal) saw minimal activity in 2025 due to political instability in those markets
- Increased competition across the value chain, especially when external markets slow, seen as a threat to prices and margins
- Urbanisation around manufacturing locations may raise environmental concerns and evolving compliance requirements

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Sustain the Core, Build the Future: protect established electrical-insulation strengths while building capability in emerging applications
- Strengthen presence in established segments (power/transmission electrical insulation) while expanding into emerging applications (e-mobility, electronics, data centres, BESS)
- Integrate innovation, sustainability and digital systems into the operating model, embedded in capital allocation, process design and execution
- Shift from material supplier to solution contributor via value-selling: engaging customers on lifecycle performance, energy implications and broader operational outcomes rather than material specs alone
- Collaboration as an operating model: joint customer visits and basket offerings across product lines instead of segments approaching customers independently
- Leverage the ALTANA/ELANTAS global network for technology transfer, troubleshooting support and access to group expertise to accelerate readiness without duplicating local development
- Platform-led innovation: extend existing chemistries into adjacent applications and selectively transfer ALTANA-network technologies rather than pursue isolated product launches
- Build leadership depth across the organisation to support future growth
- Evaluate future-ready manufacturing expansion through greenfield development and greater automation
- Advance water-based technologies to improve environmental performance while maintaining material reliability
- Strengthen process safety management and pursue energy efficiency, emission reduction and renewable energy opportunities across manufacturing operations
- Board has approved and adopted a Dividend Distribution Policy under Regulation 43A of the SEBI Listing Regulations. Dividend held flat at Rs 7.50 per equity share of Rs 10 each for FY2025, unchanged from FY2024, subject to Members' approval at the AGM. The Board did not propose any transfer to general reserves during the year under review, and share capital remained unchanged during the year. Debt-equity and debt-service/interest coverage ratios are stated as not applicable to the Company, consistent with an internally funded balance sheet.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The Company is setting up a new manufacturing facility at Taluka Vagra, District Bharuch, Gujarat (governmental approvals in process) to synergise, expand and realign its manufacturing operations for future growth. It integrated the Von Roll (India) resin and tapes business into its Pimpri operations, installing capacity for the Von Roll business at Pimpri through technology transfer, and is progressing on technology absorption/localisation of the HV resin business, having commenced manufacturing of 22 new such products at Pimpri. At Ankleshwar, infrastructure improvements de-congested and optimised the Resin Plant, increasing production capacity for PVF wire enamel, with access roads to storage/dispatch areas also improved. During the year, scrubber systems were installed at both Pimpri and Ankleshwar plants to further reduce VOC emissions, DCS rooms and software were upgraded, energy-saving projects (VFDs for cooling-tower pump motors, energy-efficient motor replacements) were executed, and new auto-packing lines were introduced to improve packaging efficiency. For 2026, the Company plans to expand the solvent recovery plant to support increased wire enamel production, which will double recovery capacity after completion. Technical improvements (debottlenecking, automation, Lean Six Sigma/Kaizen/5S) helped meet increased market demand largely without major capital expenditure.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Seven-decade legacy and technical leadership in Indian electrical insulation industry built on product quality and technical service
- Deep integration with global ALTANA/ELANTAS technical and R&D network enabling technology transfer, centralised product qualification and faster global-customer qualification cycles
- Long-standing customer relationships and strong local manufacturing combined with global technology capability
- Manufacturing execution discipline: First Time Pass Rate of 99.9% during the year, reflecting stable, system-driven plant operations
- Structured stage-gate R&D process combining technical feasibility with scale-up/operational readiness, reducing late-stage surprises

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Demand volatility across key segments — Volatility in market demand may affect order flows, production planning, and revenue visibility across key segments.
- Geographic concentration in procurement — Dependence on specific geographies for procurement could expose the supply chain to geopolitical tensions, regulatory changes, or trade restrictions, affecting raw material availability, logistics timelines, and operational continuity.
- Raw material price volatility and availability — Sharp and unexpected increases in the prices of certain key raw materials during the year added pressure, and in some cases availability became constrained, with the potential to impact production continuity, cost structures, and overall operational stability.
- Geopolitical disruption to global trade and supply chains — Ongoing conflicts in the Middle East and between Russia and Ukraine disrupted global trade flows, affected material movement, and created uncertainty across the markets the Company operates in.
- Regulatory change across markets — Changes in regulatory requirements across markets may require process adjustments, additional compliance measures, or increased costs.
- Occupational health and safety in manufacturing operations — Occupational Health and Safety risks remain inherent to manufacturing operations and require continuous vigilance to maintain employee safety and operational continuity.
- Competitive intensity when external markets slow — Increased competition across the value chain, especially when external markets slow down, may put pressure on prices and margins.
- Urbanisation around manufacturing locations — Urbanisation around manufacturing locations may result in increased environmental concerns and evolving compliance requirements.

themes.title: Import-substitution / China+1 specialty chemicals
themes.need: After the worst agrochem/chemicals year in living memory, the cycle is turning on China+1 reshoring and global pigment/dye consolidation. SUDARSCHEM is now #2 global pigment player post-Heubach; SUMICHEM posted record FY26 margins; AETHER/ANURAS/DEEPAKNTR/CLEAN add CRAMS + backward-integration; war-driven RM/freight inflation is being passed through. Q1FY27 shows the reshoring build-out actually landing: HSCL grew consolidated revenue 28% to INR 1,432cr with PAT INR 228cr (+27%) at a 22% EBITDA margin while opening three new value ladders in a single quarter (carbon nanotube 200 MTPA by Q4FY27, super-speciality carbon black 6,000 MTPA by FY28, and India's first commercial anthraquinone/carbazole plant), all self-funded with no incremental debt; TATVA grew revenue 43% YoY and delivered its first commercial-plant-scale semiconductor batch, qualified by the customer and called 'the glaring achievement of the past decade' (though commercialisation is explicitly not before Q4 CY2028); FCL tripled total income to INR 386.72cr (+165%) with Texas capacity nearly doubled to 148,000 MTPA and already running 63% on a single shift, so its next revenue leg needs only USD 1-2mn of capex.
themes.driver: Volume rebound as destocking ends; price hikes sticking; new value-ladder commissioning (HSCL CNT/carbon black) and semiconductor-materials qualification (TATVA).
